content: I'll read the test image to analyze the visual symptoms.

**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected plant part**: Banana fruits (two banana fingers shown)
- **Top banana**: Yellow skin with multiple large, irregular, dark brown to black blotches/lesions scattered across the surface; some appear slightly sunken
- **Bottom banana**: More advanced/severe infection with extensive dark necrotic areas coalescing across a large portion of the fruit surface

**Reasoning through the class options:**

| Class | Fit |
|---|---|
| **Anthracnose** | Caused by *Colletotrichum musae* — classic post-harvest fruit disease causing dark, sunken, coalescing spots on banana peel. Matches very well. |
| Bunchy_Top | Systemic viral disease affecting whole plant morphology (leaf curl, streaking) — no fruit surface spots |
| Cigar_End_Rot | Necrosis confined to the distal tip (finger end), not scattered blotches |
| Cordana_Leaf_Spot | Affects leaves with oval spots and yellow halos — not fruit |
| Panama_Disease | Vascular wilt affecting leaves/pseudostem — no surface fruit lesions |
| Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka | Leaf diseases with characteristic streaking/spotting on foliage — not fruit |

**Conclusion**: The scattered, dark, sunken, coalescing blotches on the banana fruit surface are highly characteristic of **Anthracnose** (*Colletotrichum musae*), a common post-harvest fungal disease of bananas.
